content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"The blind consensus is twofold: exegetically, fish primarily represent people/souls gathered into the kingdom through evangelism ('fishers of men,' the dragnet, the miraculous catches), with the dragnet's good and bad fish sorted at final judgment; traditionally/iconographically, the fish also represents Christ via the ICHTHYS acrostic. Secondary meanings include divine provision, the sign of Jonah, Eucharistic use, and prophetic imagery of men as fish caught by powers (Hab 1:14, Jer 16:16).","book_summary":"The book defines the fish as a person in the sea of nations — clean or unclean — who is gathered and sorted at the harvest, with fishers of men drawing the catch from the sea in the net. It cross-references the sea as the realm of nations/peoples.","consensus_core_identification":"Fish = people (souls) in the world gathered by gospel mission and sorted at eschatological judgment (with a parallel traditional identification of the fish emblem as Christ via ICHTHYS).","book_core_identification":"Fish = a person among the nations (the sea), gathered by fishers of men and sorted (clean/unclean, good/bad) at the harvest/judgment.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"None material. The book fuses the evangelism reading (Matt 4:19) and the judgment-sorting reading (Matt 13:47-48) into a single identification, and adds the 'sea of nations' framing via Hab 1:14 — all of which the consensus already recognizes (Response A explicitly lists the prophetic 'men as fish' texts and the dragnet sorting). The book simply omits the post-biblical ICHTHYS/Christ emblem, but omission of an iconographic tradition in a biblical glossary is not a boundary rejection.","material_contradiction":"None. The book does not deny the Christ/ICHTHYS tradition; it addresses the intra-biblical symbol, where the consensus itself says the 'people gathered for the kingdom' reading is exegetically primary.","rationale":"Reduced to minimum cores, both identify fish as people drawn from the world/sea by gospel fishing and separated at judgment. Responses A and B make this the primary exegetical meaning, and C and D list it as a common alternative; the dragnet sorting and Habakkuk's 'men as fishes of the sea' are explicitly present in the consensus. The book's 'sea of nations' phrasing is a systematizing detail consistent with the consensus reading of the dragnet 'cast into the sea, gathered of every kind.' Nothing in the entry replaces or contradicts the consensus referent, so this is MATCH rather than REFINED or DIVERGENT.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue the book narrows the symbol by silently excluding the ICHTHYS/Christ identification, which two responses (C, D) treat as the dominant meaning, making the relation REFINED (BOOK_SUBSET). But glossary silence is not exclusion, and the consensus itself acknowledges the Christ reading is post-biblical tradition while the 'people caught for the kingdom' reading is the primary meaning of the biblical text — exactly the book's terrain.","confidence":"high"}
